title: [D7 Observability] Metrics and reconciliation over the whole pipeline
summary: `concept/07`'s Observability section has an implementation: seven plain views in `sql/migrations/0021_pipeline_observability.sql` (ingest ledger, feed staleness, run metrics, failure counts, escalation counts, retrieval metrics, pipeline reconciliation), a reader module `helena.status` that checks each row against itself and refuses every rate over an empty denominator, and `uv run scripts/status.py` — `helena status`, also `make status` — which renders all of it beside the two counters earlier increments already built (`helena_signal_retention_rejections` from 0009, `helena_analytical_emission_counts` from 0020). No metrics store, no exporter, no scrape endpoint, no dashboard and no hosted tracer: `docs/decisions/0038-pipeline-metrics-and-reconciliation.md` records that as an egress decision under `concept/instruction.md` §3 rather than a configuration detail, and `docs/runbook.md` §13 explains the numbers for an operator.
assumption_validated: THAT EVERY NUMBER `concept/07` NAMES IS DERIVABLE FROM THE SINGLE STORE IN PLAIN SQL, with no second store of derived numbers and no tracer — demonstrated against the pinned engine over assessments written by the real writer, a capture ingested through the real path and a snapshot loaded by the real loader (ADR-0038 §7). The corollary the increment also settled is that a rate cannot live in SQL: a view cannot refuse a division over an empty denominator, so `0.0` would ship as the fact 'the boundary dropped nothing' / 'triage escalates nothing' / 'this model is free'. Every view therefore exposes a numerator and a denominator and stops, and all seven rates are properties on `helena.status` models that raise — the rule `helena.context.RetentionRejections.rate` set in task 12. NOT VALIDATED, and ADR-0038 §7 says so: that this is the right *set* of numbers. No deployment has been watched with it, there are no thresholds, no alerting and no baseline.
makes_buildable: Task 49 (the conformance suite) gets the countability half of `concept/instruction.md` §7 as queryable rows rather than as an assertion over Python objects: `helena_analytical_failure_counts` is one row per typed failure reason, `helena_analytical_escalation_counts` breaks the escalation rate down by trigger, and a must-never-happen entry like 'a budget-truncated run returning normal' now has an engine-side witness. Task 50 (architectural boundary tests) gets seven new relations whose `Layer:` and `Read by:` heads are already written, and the layering argument for why the reconciliation is two views rather than one (ADR-0038 §3) is the case its `layering_violations` check exists to protect. Task 52 (end to end) gets its acceptance readout: `uv run scripts/status.py --captures data/ingest` is the one command that shows the whole pipeline's terms reconciling after an ingest → context → enrich → triage → analyse → emit run, and `PipelineReconciliation.unaccounted` is the number that says whether anything was lost. Task 53 (durability) gets counters that survive a restart to compare across one.

Its rendering is covered by tests/test_status.py instead.

escalations.detail: Six applied migrations gained `Read by:` lines naming the seven new views — 0003, 0004, 0006, 0013, 0018 and 0020 — which tests/test_view_layering.py requires of every relation that is read. The checksum ledger is over the bytes, so a store migrated before 0021 must be dropped and re-migrated. Same standing cost as the five earlier retrofits; docs/runbook.md §5 is where that list lives.

invariant_conflicts: THE TASK'S THIRD STEP — 'write a reconciliation view comparing capture record count, normalized rows, quarantined rows, context rows and emitted rows' — IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AS ONE VIEW WITHOUT BREAKING THE LAYERING INVARIANT, and was not implemented as one. `concept/instruction.md` §2 and `concept/03-architecture.md`: an analytical view references the signal layer, never the flatten layer and never the source directly. Those five terms live in three view layers and one of them is not in the engine at all (the capture record count is a property of the retained file, `helena.normalizer.Capture.record_count`). One view over all five would read the source layer from the analytical layer, which `helena.migrations.layering_violations` fails. Implemented instead as two views plus the join in Python: `helena_ingest_ledger` (source layer, over the source counters) and `helena_analytical_pipeline_reconciliation` (signal and analytical), with `helena.status.PipelineReconciliation` as the one object that holds all five terms and checks them against each other — the shape `helena.normalizer.IngestCounts` already has, and for its reason: the numbers deliberately come from different places, and that is what makes the check worth running. ADR-0038 §3 has the two rejected alternatives and why each was worse than the conflict.
deferred: ANY THRESHOLD, ALERT OR BASELINE. `helena status` prints numbers and does not decide which of them are bad — it is explicitly not a health check (ADR-0038 §6). Nothing watches it, nothing pages, and there is no 'normal' to compare against, because `concept/01`'s question — is the assisted pipeline better than the deterministic baseline in accuracy, escalation rate, latency and cost? — is a question about an evaluation corpus that does not exist yet (task 54).

MODEL-QUALITY METRICS BEYOND WHAT THE STORE ALREADY WITNESSES. The task's wording includes 'model-quality metrics'; what exists is the retry count, the typed-failure breakdown, the verdict count and the cost and latency distribution per model and per model version. Accuracy is not among them and cannot be: there is no ground truth in the store to score a verdict against. Task 54 is where that starts.

ANY EGRESS OF THESE NUMBERS. No OTLP exporter, no Prometheus endpoint, no metrics push, no dashboard, no hosted tracer — each is a second egress channel or a new HTTP surface and therefore an escalation under `concept/instruction.md` §3, not a convenience. ADR-0038 §1 and its rejected-alternatives list are what a later increment has to argue against.

MATERIALIZING ANY OF THE SEVEN. All are plain views, read occasionally as numbers, never streamed or joined from; two could not be materialized in any case (`helena_reference_feed_staleness` computes `age_seconds` from `now()` outside a WHERE clause, and `helena_analytical_pipeline_reconciliation` stands on the emission count, which stands on a view that cannot source a streaming job at all).

A TIME WINDOW ON ANY METRIC. Every view aggregates the whole store — there is no 'last hour' or 'since' parameter anywhere, and `max(assessed_at)` is the only temporal column a reader gets. An operator narrows with their own WHERE clause in psql; `helena status` has no flag for it.

COUNTING WHAT WAS EMITTED, as opposed to what is emittable. Unchanged from task 47 and for ADR-0037 §3's reason: nothing records that a message was produced, so the reconciliation's last term is named `emittable` for what it holds (ADR-0038 §4).
lessons: A RATE BELONGS IN PYTHON AND ITS NUMERATOR AND DENOMINATOR BELONG IN SQL. A view cannot refuse a division, so a rate column would ship `0.0` as a fact in exactly the situation the number is being read to diagnose — nothing has run. Seven rates in this increment raise instead, and `helena.status.render` prints the refusal's own sentence where the number would have been rather than catching it and printing a zero. This is the same call task 12's `RetentionRejections.rate` and the normalizer's `QuarantineCounts.rate` already made.

`helena.status` CANNOT BE FOLDED INTO `helena.observability`, for a mechanical reason and not an aesthetic one: the metrics read `helena.enrichment`'s feed statuses so that `ok` / `stale` / `missing` are not respelled a fourth time, and `helena.enrichment` imports `helena.observability` for the redactor. One module is an import cycle. It is in `tests/test_package_layout.py`'s SUPPORT_MODULES rather than COMPONENT_MODULES because it is not a stage — it reads every stage's counters and owns none of them.

THE FIVE TERMS OF AN END-TO-END RECONCILIATION DO NOT FIT IN ONE VIEW IN A LAYERED SCHEMA, and the right answer is two views and an object that joins them, not a widened invariant. Widening `MAY_READ["analytical"]` to include `source` would license every future analytical view to skip the signal layer; a row-count view parked in the `flatten` layer would be formally legal and dishonest, since that layer is the flattening of nested observations and a count is not that.

WHAT RECONCILES AND WHAT MERELY REPORTS HAVE TO BE SEPARATED OR THE CHECK FIRES ON A HEALTHY PIPELINE. Refused: normalized + quarantined = admitted; admitted no greater than capture records; context records no greater than normalized; verdicts + typed failures = runs; cache hits + live queries = steps; escalations by trigger summing to escalations. Merely reported: `unaggregated` (a normalized event with no `ip` layer or an unparseable `ts` produces a flatten row the tumble drops — a fact about the input, and a pipeline that hid it could not tell anybody the input changed), and `emittable` against `assessments`, which differ legitimately whenever a pass escalated: two runs, one message.

AN ABSENT CAPTURE DIRECTORY IS SAID, NEVER DEFAULTED TO 0. How many records existed is a property of the retained file and of nothing else, because the broker is consume-once and restart-volatile, so `--captures` is optional and `0` would report a deployment that had lost every record it ever ingested. `PipelineReconciliation.unaccounted` raises when no capture directory was read.

A REPORT OVER A STORE STAMPS ONE MOMENT, AND IT HAS TO BE PASSED IN. `helena.status.report` takes `read_at` rather than calling `now()` itself: every staleness number in the result is relative to a moment, and a report that stamped itself would stamp a different moment than the `now()` the engine used inside the staleness view.

A MIGRATION THAT ADDS RELATIONS HAS TO EXTEND THE INVENTORY PINS IN OTHER TEST MODULES, and the full suite is the only thing that finds them -- this is the third increment in a row to learn it (task 46 recorded the class, task 47 hit one pin, this one hit two). The pins are deliberate friction and they are in modules the increment otherwise has no reason to open: tests/test_enriched.py holds the ORDERED list of analytical objects that read something (ordered, so it fails rather than merely being fragile), and tests/test_enrichment.py holds the reference layer's table/view inventory, as tests/test_context.py does for the signal layer. Adding a view in a layer means editing that layer's inventory in the same increment.
failed_approaches: A SINGLE RECONCILIATION VIEW OVER ALL FIVE TERMS, which is what the task's third step asks for. It cannot be written without reading the source layer from the analytical layer; `helena.migrations.layering_violations` fails it. See the invariant conflict above.

WIDENING `MAY_READ["analytical"]` TO INCLUDE `source` so that the single view would be legal. Rejected before it was written: it is an edit to the invariant to make one view convenient, and it silently licenses every future analytical view to skip the signal layer.

A ROW-COUNT VIEW IN THE `flatten` LAYER (which may read `source`) for the signal layer and then the analytical layer to read in turn. Formally legal and rejected as dishonest — the flatten layer is the flattening of nested observations (ADR-0015), and a row count is not that. Compliance dressed up.

RATE COLUMNS IN SQL, and a `metrics` table written by the pipeline. The first ships `0.0` as a fact over an empty denominator; the second is a second store of derived numbers that can disagree with the rows they were derived from, against `concept/instruction.md` §2's one store.

A HOSTED TRACER (Langfuse, LangSmith, OTLP to a vendor) and a PROMETHEUS ENDPOINT, both rejected on the note's own terms rather than on ergonomics: the first is a second egress channel carrying prompts and retrieved provider text, needing its own send policy, its own disclosure record and a second vendor's data-handling terms; the second is a new HTTP surface that would answer *fewer* questions than the SQL, because a counter loses the version set, the model identity and the context reference — exactly what an audit needs.
next_session_should_know: D7 IS COMPLETE AND THIS TASK'S LANDING IS UNUSUAL — read the `reconstructed` block below before trusting the shape of this report. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS `status.report(connection, identity, read_at=..., captures=...) -> Status`, with `helena.status.render(status) -> str` for the terminal and `scripts/status.py` / `make status` as the operator surface; `--captures DIR` is optional and its absence is reported rather than defaulted to 0. (2) THE SEVEN VIEWS ARE IN `sql/migrations/0021` and the module exports their names as constants (`INGEST_LEDGER_VIEW` … `PIPELINE_RECONCILIATION_VIEW`); the two counters it also reads are NOT re-declared there — the rejection rate comes through `helena.context.ContextStore.rejections` and the emittable count through `helena.sink.SinkStore.pending`, because a second copy of either would be a second number to disagree with the first. (3) SIX APPLIED MIGRATIONS WERE RETROFITTED (`Read by:` only), so a store migrated before 0021 must be dropped and re-migrated. (4) EVERY RATE RAISES OVER AN EMPTY DENOMINATOR. If you read one of these models, handle the refusal or let it propagate — do not catch it and print 0, which is the failure mode the design exists to prevent. (5) THE TASK'S 'ONE RECONCILIATION VIEW' STEP CONFLICTS WITH THE LAYERING INVARIANT and was implemented as two views plus a Python join. If a later task wants to simplify that, read ADR-0038 §3 first: both obvious simplifications were considered and are worse. (6) NOTHING IS WATCHED, NOTHING ALERTS, AND THERE IS NO BASELINE. Adding an exporter, a scrape endpoint or a dashboard is an egress escalation under `concept/instruction.md` §3, not a convenience. (7) THE RUNNER'S OWN VIEW OF THIS TASK WAS 'failed' UNTIL THIS LANDING. `prds/session.json`'s iteration 45 records a genuine failed iteration — exit 143, a zero-byte log, no report — and that entry is left as it stands, because it happened. `prd.json`, `progress.txt`, `session-memory.json` and `session.json`'s `currentTaskIndex` were updated by the landing session under §4, *Landing without the runner*. The next task is 49.
